title: Shan seed-treadle loom
summary: In the Shan hills of Myanmar, cotton cloth is woven on a heavy loom that stands close to the ground. The weaver works the treadles with her toes; they are often made from large pierced wild-bean seeds. A shuttle of cotton thread crosses the opened threads to make plain, striped and checked cloth.
howToPlay: Pick a cotton colour from the bobbins and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored across and down the cloth.
Copy the cloth shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is mirrored both left to right and top to bottom, so each shape is woven on up to four squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its cotton colour both match the cloth you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: The Shan region lies in eastern Myanmar, where families have long woven their own cotton cloth. An early twentieth-century account describes a heavy loom close to the ground with treadles made of large seeds, and a weaver who could finish several yards of plain cloth in a day.
